key_insight: Optimizing the periodic geometry of hyperbolic surface codes can double the code distance and quadruple efficiency at fixed qubit count, rate, and parity-check weight.
engineering_relevance: The work points to more scalable fault-tolerant quantum hardware by combining high-efficiency error correction with a modular layout that reduces routing complexity.
method: Constructed finite families of hyperbolic surface codes with bounded local geometry.
Introduced a topology-aware partitioning algorithm to split codes into bounded planar modules.
Evaluated modular and monolithic layouts with circuit-level Monte Carlo simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports finite-size threshold estimates from circuit-level Monte Carlo studies and notes that tripling long-range gate error only mildly lowers the estimated thresholds.
watch_item: The modular approach still depends on managing long-range communication and may face implementation overhead in hardware with higher interconnect error rates.
paper_title: Geometry-optimized hyperbolic codes for modular fault-tolerant quantum architectures
